answer: An agent economy can resist sybil attacks by requiring each identity to stake a small refundable deposit and earn reputation through attested work before gaining full transaction rights. Like a river that only lets proven boats pass, new agents start on a narrow ledge with capped volume and no voting weight. A shared lagoon of peer attestations records completed jobs, so spinning up many fake identities costs real stake and time while earning no trust, making sybil attacks expensive and slow to scale.
